evals.prompt: I have an Android package id com.vendor.router and I do not want to install adb, jadx, or apktool with Homebrew. Create a Docker-based runbook to pull the Play-installed split APKs from my phone and decompile them.
evals.expected_output: Explains authorized scope, wireless ADB pairing, Docker ADB shell, pull-package-apks, no-network analysis shell, signature/hash verification, jadx with all split APKs, apktool on base.apk, and artifact hygiene.

evals.prompt: I downloaded a .xapk file from APKPure for an app I own. How should I verify it and decompile it without trusting it blindly?
evals.expected_output: Provides APKPure search/detail/download/version URL patterns, treats XAPK as an untrusted ZIP bundle, rejects HTML challenge pages, verifies APKs with apksigner, hashes the bundle and splits, recommends signer comparison against a Play-installed copy, runs jadx over all APKs, apktool on base.apk, and warns not to commit APK/decompiled source.

evals.prompt: Use the APK artifacts from a previous session to write a static-analysis checklist for finding local API endpoints and auth clues.
evals.expected_output: Uses the generic artifact trail without vendor-specific references, keeps the Docker split between ADB and analysis, searches manifest/network config/native strings/JADX/apktool output, looks for endpoint/auth/token clues, and distinguishes static candidates from observed endpoints.
